public.case.title: Why a spreadsheet and an inbox are not enough
public.case.lede: Most banks keep their obligations in a spreadsheet and follow regulatory news in an inbox.
public.case.body: That holds up until a reviewer asks what an obligation said two years ago and who decided that it applied to your Norwegian entity. Compliance Watch overwrites nothing, so both answers are still there when someone asks.
public.case.version.title: Earlier wording is lost
public.case.version.body: Once a cell is edited, nothing shows what it said before or when the old wording stopped applying.
public.case.decision.title: A status carries no decision
public.case.decision.body: A cell marked as compliant does not record who reached that conclusion or what evidence they relied on.
public.case.coverage.title: Coverage cannot be shown
public.case.coverage.body: An inbox shows what reached you, but it cannot show that nothing relevant was missed.
public.what.title: What Compliance Watch does
public.what.inventory.title: Every obligation, with its history
public.what.inventory.body: Each obligation keeps all its versions with the dates they took effect. You can read the wording that applied on any given date and see what changed between versions, sentence by sentence.
public.what.watch.title: Agents find changes, and your bank decides
public.what.watch.body: Research agents check each source on its own schedule and file what they find as proposals, because a proposal is the only way anything enters the shared library.
public.what.ask.title: Answers that cite their source
public.what.ask.body: Answers are drawn only from the inventory and cite it. Pending changes are flagged, and when the inventory holds no answer you are told so instead of getting a guess.
public.what.evidence.title: What applies, and where you stand
public.what.evidence.body: Applicability and compliance status are recorded for each legal entity, gaps get an owner and a date, and a second person in your bank signs off.
public.method.title: Every change takes the same six steps
public.method.sighted.name: Sighted.
public.method.sighted.body: A regulator publishes, and an agent picks it up at the source's next scheduled check.
public.method.proposed.name: Proposed.
public.method.proposed.body: The agent drafts the change against the wording currently in force.
public.method.confirmed.name: Confirmed.
public.method.confirmed.body: A second agent, with its own definition and key, checks the draft against the source. No agent can confirm a proposal it made itself.
public.method.applied.name: Applied.
public.method.applied.body: The new version enters the library with its effective date, and the previous version stays readable.
public.method.assessed.name: Assessed.
public.method.assessed.body: Your bank decides whether the change applies to you and where you stand.
public.method.signedOff.name: Signed off.
public.method.signedOff.body: A second person in your bank signs off, and the evidence for the change is closed.
public.method.footnote: A fact confirmed this way names both agents and is never presented as checked by a person. What it means for your bank is decided and signed off by your own people.
public.zones.title: What banks share, and what stays with you
public.zones.library.title: The shared library
public.zones.library.body: The library holds instruments, provisions, obligations and their effective dates, each linked to its source. Every bank reads the same library, so a correction reaches all of them at once.
public.zones.door.label: Proposals only
public.zones.door.body: The only way in, checked by a second reviewer
public.zones.yours.title: Your zone
public.zones.yours.body: Applicability, compliance status, gaps, evidence and sign-off belong to your bank and are never visible outside it.
public.zones.footnote: Your bank's content is kept out of logs and error reports, and we send none of it to a model apart from the questions your people type into Ask, which your bank can switch off.

public.assurance.title: What your vendor review will ask
public.assurance.access.body: Passkeys are the only way in, so there is no password to phish and no reset link to intercept.
public.assurance.fourEyes.body: Approvals, sign-off and changes to your scope need a second person, and the database refuses the same person in both roles rather than flagging it afterwards.
public.assurance.isolation.body: Row-level security in the database keeps each bank's data out of every other bank's reach, whatever the query.
public.assurance.models.body: Every model call is logged, and content fetched from the web is treated as material to read, never as an instruction to follow.
public.assurance.ledger.body: Every change is stored beside the version it replaced, and its audit entry is written in the same transaction.
public.assurance.retention.body: A record is deleted in full ten years after it was last used.
public.assurance.leaving.body: Two people approve the exit, your bank's data becomes read-only while the final export is taken, and then every row is deleted, including the audit trail.
public.assurance.pack.body: Compliance Watch is an ICT third-party service under DORA, and the pack covers what that brings: the sub-processor register with locations, data flows for each zone, recovery objectives, the incident runbook and the exit plan.
public.questions.title: Common questions
public.questions.ai.a: Agents find changes and file drafts of them as proposals, but they decide nothing for your bank. A fact that a second agent confirms is labelled as machine-confirmed, and what it means for you is decided by your people.
public.questions.oneEntity.q: Can we start with one legal entity?
public.questions.oneEntity.a: You can, and widening the scope later is a request that a second person approves, with both steps recorded.
public.questions.whoSees.a: Only your own people see them. The shared library holds public facts, and your assessments stay in your zone.
public.questions.libraryWrong.q: What if the library is wrong?
public.questions.libraryWrong.a: Report it on the record, and the report stays inside your bank. The agents check each library record against its source on every run and correct it through an ordinary proposal.
public.questions.getIn.a: Your administrator sends an invitation, and each person registers a passkey on their own device. There is no password to set.
public.questions.cost.a: Pricing is agreed with each bank when access is arranged.
public.request.title: Access is by invitation.
public.request.invited: If your bank already uses bleqq, your administrator sends the invitation.
public.request.introduce: If it does not, write to us and we will arrange an introduction.
